result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers handle body size, heading scale, mobile reduction, caption and code well, and both give pasteable custom properties. A caps paragraphs at 65ch. B never sets a max-width on the article column, so it fails the measure requirement outright, and that settles the comparison. B's token-based line-heights and its notes on assumptions are nice touches, but they don't make up for the missing measure. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give sound type scales: body is 16–17px, mobile h1 is about 0.7–0.75 of desktop, headings have tight leading and code uses a monospace stack at the right size. B caps the measure with max-width: 65ch on paragraphs and a narrower pull quote, while A sets no column width at all, which is a significant omission for an article template. A's tokenization is a bit more complete because line-heights are also custom properties, but that doesn't make up for the missing measure.
